extracted.intended_audience: researchers conducting systematic reviews/meta-analyses in mental health and cardiovascular epidemiology (PTSD and hypertension)
extracted.subtask_description: A condition-specific systematic review and meta-analysis protocol (PTSD and early-onset hypertension) prepared following PRISMA-P guidance and for registration in PROSPERO; hosted as an OSF registration and released under CC BY 4.0. The protocol defines exposure (PTSD, including ICD-11 Complex PTSD and pharmacological treatments), outcome (early-onset hypertension), and downstream comparisons (long-term cardiovascular and all-cause mortality vs mid-life onset).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to PRISMA-P guidance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocol designed in line with PRISMA-P (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic review and Meta-Analysis Protocols) standards; this implies inclusion of standard protocol elements such as eligibility criteria, information sources, search strategy, data management, selection process, data collection, outcomes, risk-of-bias assessment, synthesis methods, and plans for reporting. The registration indicates the protocol was prepared specifically to meet PRISMA-P expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register protocol in PROSPERO
rubrics_metrics.description: Protocol has been prepared for registration in PROSPERO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and submit materials required by PROSPERO (e.g., title, objectives, methods, inclusion criteria, outcomes) so the systematic review protocol is publicly registered prior to conduct to enhance transparency and reduce reporting bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition-specific systematic review and meta-analysis design
rubrics_metrics.description: This project hosts the full protocol for a condition-specific systematic review and meta-analysis investigating the association between post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), including ICD-11 Complex PTSD and its pharmacological treatments, and the risk of early-onset hypertension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the review to be condition-specific (PTSD and Complex PTSD), explicitly include pharmacological treatments as exposures where relevant, define early-onset hypertension as the primary outcome, and use appropriate meta-analytic methods when studies are sufficiently homogeneous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify downstream comparative outcomes (long-term morbidity and mortality)
rubrics_metrics.description: The review will also evaluate whether early-onset hypertension in PTSD populations is associated with higher long-term cardiovascular and all-cause mortality compared with typical mid-life onset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include planned analyses comparing long-term cardiovascular outcomes and all-cause mortality between early-onset hypertension cases in PTSD populations and typical mid-life onset cases; specify data extraction items, subgroup or sensitivity analyses, and approaches to handle confounding and follow-up differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open registration and licensing (OSF/CC BY 4.0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Protocol hosted as an OSF registration (osf-registrations) and released under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make full protocol and registration metadata publicly available via OSF, include machine-readable metadata (e.g., OSF registration DOI), and apply an open license (CC BY 4.0) to facilitate reuse, transparency, and discoverability.
